content:
Ivy Park: hey folks — accepted the org invite but the repo https://github.com/redwood/bootcamp-starter shows 404 and `git clone` fails with permission denied. who should i poke? :slightly_smiling_face:
Noah Kim: welcome Ivy! first check: did you enable 2FA on your GitHub account? Redwood requires it for org access.
Ivy Park: i set up 2FA earlier today. how can i tell if the org recognized it?
AccessBot: Hi Ivy — to verify: visit https://github.com/orgs/redwood/sso or run `gh auth status`. If the org still blocks you reply `ping-access` and an admin will inspect.
Ivy Park: `gh auth status` shows i'm logged in as ivypark. Org page still 404 though.
Rina Das: a couple possibilities: (1) your work email on GH isn't verified, (2) SSO authorization not completed, or (3) team mapping didn't run. Ivy, is your GitHub account email ivy@redwood.com?
Ivy Park: yes, that email is on my account but it was secondary. i've verified it now and reauthorized SSO.
Noah Kim: thanks — i'm checking the org console. Ivy is a member but not assigned to `eng-interns` due to a mapping hiccup. adding you to `eng-interns` with Write access now.
Noah Kim: assigned. refresh the repo page and try cloning again.
Ivy Park: repo visible now! cloning works too. quick follow-up: i tried `git push` to `main` and got "remote: error: protected branch". is that expected?
Owen Brooks: yes, main is protected across onboarding repos. create a feature branch and open a PR. Also FYI, committer email should be your work address for CI checks.
Ivy Park: ah — my local git used my personal email. i'll update `git config user.email "ivy@redwood.com"` and amend the commit. thanks for the help! :tada:
Noah Kim: one last thing — if anyone else runs into a 404 after SSO, try verifying emails and then ping #new-hires so we can check team mapping quickly.
